ADM-001.q: What is the number and effective date of the current Tax Administration Law?
ADM-001.e: The 2025 Tax Administration Law, No. 108/2025/QH15, takes effect from 01/7/2026.
ADM-001.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: The 2025 Tax Administration Law (108/2025/QH15) replaces Law 38/2019/QH14 from 01/07/2026 – alongside its guidance (Decree 252/2026, Circular 89/2026) and the new invoicing decree (Decree 254/2026).
Distractors: B is the replaced law; C has the wrong date; D is the CIT Law.

ADM-002.q: Match each document with its guidance content (effective 01/7/2026):
ADM-002.e: The new tax administration and invoice documents all take effect from 01/7/2026.
ADM-002.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15 and its implementing texts.
Analysis: Decree 252/2026 – details the Tax Administration Law (replacing Decree 126/2020); Circular 89/2026 – procedures and forms (replacing Circular 80/2021); Decree 254/2026 – e-invoices and documents (replacing Decree 123/2020); Circular 91/2026 – e-invoice guidance (replacing Circular 78/2021). All effective 01/07/2026.

ADM-003.q: Under the 2025 Tax Administration Law, a taxpayer finding errors in a tax return may file a supplementary return within:
o: 5 years from the filing deadline of the period with the error (before an inspection/audit decision is announced)
ADM-003.e: Law 108/2025/QH15 shortens the supplementary filing period from 10 years (2019 Law) to 5 years.
ADM-003.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: The supplementary filing window shrinks from 10 years (2019 Law) to 5 years from the original filing deadline of the erroneous period, and must precede an on-site audit decision. It aligns with assessment and penalty limitation periods.
Distractors: B is the old rule; C and D have no basis.
Note: Review old-period errors early – after 5 years even downward corrections are barred.

ADM-004.q: Tax debts outstanding up to 30/6/2026 are handled under the 2025 Tax Administration Law.
ADM-004.e: True under the transitional rules; exemptions, reductions and non-collection arising before 01/7/2026 continue under the 2019 Law.
ADM-004.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Tax debts up to 30/06/2026 are handled (suspension, write-off, enforcement…) under the 2025 Law once effective; exemption, reduction and non-collection cases arising before 01/07/2026 continue under the 2019 Law – avoiding adverse retroactivity.

ADM-005.q: Documents and decisions issued automatically by the tax management system are signed with the tax authority's digital signature and have the same legal value as paper documents.
ADM-005.e: True. The 2025 Law promotes digital transformation and automation in tax administration.
ADM-005.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; E-Transactions Law 20/2023/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 2025 Law recognises documents and decisions issued automatically by the tax system, digitally signed by the authority, as legally equivalent to paper – the basis for automated notices and decisions (e.g., interest notices, automatic refunds).

ADM-006.q: Automatic refunds, exemptions and reductions are implemented on a roadmap based on data, risk criteria and information security requirements.
ADM-006.e: True. This is new in the 2025 Tax Administration Law.
ADM-006.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Automatic refunds, exemptions and reductions are new, phased in based on data, risk criteria and information security – not every case is automated at once; coverage expands with data readiness.

ADM-007.q: Select ALL criteria the tax authority uses to segment taxpayers under the 2025 Tax Administration Law:
o: Distance from the office to the tax authority
ADM-007.e: Segmentation lets the authority apply appropriate management measures, priority and risk assessment.
ADM-007.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Taxpayer segmentation criteria: (A) sector and business model; (B) legal form and ownership; (C) revenue size and budget contribution; (D) compliance history – supporting risk-based management.
Distractors: (E) female headcount and (F) distance are irrelevant to compliance risk.

ADM-008.q: Select ALL prohibited acts added or clarified by the 2025 Tax Administration Law:
o: Abusing position to disclose or leak taxpayer information unlawfully
Unlawfully creating electronic invoices or vouchers
Unauthorised access, alteration or destruction of taxpayer information systems
Filing supplementary returns within the time limit
ADM-008.e: Supplementary filings and proper deferral requests are taxpayers' rights.
ADM-008.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Added or clarified prohibitions: (A) abusing office to disclose taxpayer data; (B) unlawfully creating e-invoices or documents; (C) unauthorised access, alteration or destruction of tax information systems – reflecting digital-era risks.
Distractors: (D) timely supplementary filing and (E) lawful deferral requests are taxpayer rights.

ADM-009.q: The filing deadline for monthly-filed taxes is:
o: The 20th of the month following the month the obligation arises
The last day of the following month
ADM-009.e: Monthly: by the 20th of the next month; quarterly: by the last day of the first month of the next quarter.
ADM-009.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly returns are due by the 20th of the next month; quarterly by the last day of the next quarter's first month; annual finalisation by the last day of the third month; per-transaction by the 10th day (ADM-011).
Distractors: B confuses it with per-transaction; C is the quarterly deadline; D has no basis.

ADM-010.q: The Q3/2026 VAT return deadline (last day of the first month of the next quarter is Saturday 31/10/2026) is:
ADM-010.e: A deadline falling on a day off moves to the next working day: 02/11/2026.
ADM-010.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: The Q3 deadline is the last day of October = 31/10/2026 (Saturday). A deadline on a day off ends on the next working day – Monday 02/11/2026.
Distractors: B – filing early isn't required; C ignores the shift; D confuses it with monthly filing.

ADM-011.q: Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, the deadline for per-transaction tax returns is:
o: No later than the 10th day after the obligation arises (counting from the next day)
The same as the quarterly deadline
ADM-011.e: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP changes the count: the 10th day from the day after the obligation arises.
ADM-011.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Per-transaction returns are due by the 10th day counted from the day after the tax point – a clearer count (excluding the tax-point day). Used for contractor tax, capital and property transfers…
Distractors: B is the monthly deadline; C and D are wrong.

ADM-012.q: Under Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC, a taxpayer may file VAT quarterly when:
o: Total revenue from goods/services in the preceding year was VND 50 billion or less, or it has just started business
Prior-year revenue was below VND 100 billion
Charter capital is below VND 10 billion
ADM-012.e: Article 19 of Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC: the 50 billion threshold; new businesses may choose quarterly filing.
ADM-012.x:
Basis: Article 19 of Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Taxpayers may file VAT quarterly if prior-year sales revenue is ≤ 50 billion VND, or if newly operating; above that, monthly filing applies.
Distractors: B has the wrong threshold; C and D aren't criteria.

ADM-013.q: An enterprise switching from monthly to quarterly VAT filing must submit a request by 31/01 of the year quarterly filing starts and apply it for the whole calendar year.
ADM-013.x:
Basis: Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. To switch from monthly to quarterly, submit a request by 31/01 of the year of change; the period stays fixed for the whole calendar year – avoiding mid-year changes that complicate reconciliation.

ADM-014.q: E-commerce platforms with online ordering and payment functions must withhold, file and pay tax on behalf of household/individual businesses on the platform.
ADM-014.e: True. If a platform lacks either function, household businesses file and pay themselves.
ADM-014.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Platforms with both ordering and payment functions control sellers' cash flows, so they withhold, file and pay VAT and PIT for household/individual sellers (PIT-109). If either function is missing, sellers self-file.

ADM-015.q: Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, if a Vietnamese enterprise has already withheld tax on a purchase of services from a foreign supplier, the e-commerce platform does not withhold again on the same transaction.
ADM-015.e: True. The Vietnamese enterprise sends the tax payment receipt to the platform to avoid double withholding.
ADM-015.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. To avoid double withholding, once a Vietnamese company has withheld tax on a purchase from a foreign supplier, it sends the payment receipt to the platform, which then doesn't withhold again on that transaction.

ADM-016.q: Foreign investors may remit profits abroad only after the enterprise has fulfilled financial obligations, filed audited financial statements and the CIT finalisation, and has no tax debt at the time of remittance.
ADM-016.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Conditions for remitting profits abroad: financial obligations fulfilled, audited FS and CIT finalisation filed, and no tax debt at the time – securing revenue before cash leaves Vietnam.

ADM-017.q: A foreign-invested enterprise with accumulated losses remaining after loss carry-forward may still remit current-year profits abroad.
ADM-017.e: False. Decree 252/2026/ND-CP does not allow remitting current-year profits while accumulated losses remain after carry-forward.
ADM-017.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. With accumulated losses remaining after loss carry-forward, current-year profit must first cover those losses; current-year profit can't be remitted abroad in that case.

ADM-018.q: Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, an exit ban is lifted when the taxpayer has paid part of the debt and the remaining tax debt is below VND 500 million for enterprises/cooperatives (below VND 50 million for individuals/household businesses).
ADM-018.e: True. These are the new thresholds for lifting exit bans.
ADM-018.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. An exit ban is lifted when the taxpayer pays part and the remaining debt falls below 500 million VND (enterprises, cooperatives) or 50 million VND (individuals, household businesses) – a proportionate mechanism rather than full payment.

ADM-019.q: The buyer must file supplementary returns when a competent authority concludes the seller used illegal invoices, even for periods already inspected or audited.
ADM-019.e: True under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP. A major risk when buying from opaque suppliers.
ADM-019.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. When a seller is found to have used illegal invoices, the buyer must amend (reduce input VAT and expenses) even for audited periods – an exception to the usual bar.
Note: Supplier due diligence (KYC, tax ID status, real operations) is a key control.

ADM-020.q: The VAT allocation rules for construction, real-estate transfers and production in provinces other than the head office, under the transitional provisions of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, apply only until 31/12/2026.
ADM-020.e: True. Enterprises with out-of-province production sites or projects should watch for guidance applying from 2027.
ADM-020.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. VAT allocation to provinces hosting construction, property transfers or production outside the head-office province continues transitionally until 31/12/2026; businesses should watch guidance for 2027 onwards.

ADM-021.q: From 01/7/2025, personal identification numbers are used instead of tax codes for individuals and dependants.
ADM-021.e: True. Enterprises must update employees' and dependants' ID numbers in PIT records.
ADM-021.x:
Basis: Circular 86/2024/TT-BTC on tax registration.
Analysis: True. From 01/07/2025, the personal identification number (citizen ID) replaces individuals' and dependants' tax IDs. Employers must update IDs in PIT records, withholding certificates and dependant registrations.

ADM-022.q: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP on administrative penalties for tax and invoices (and its amendments) remains in force after 01/7/2026 until replaced.
ADM-022.e: True under the transitional provisions of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
ADM-022.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 125/2020 on tax and invoice penalties (as amended by Decrees 102/2021, 310/2025…) remains in force after 01/07/2026 until replaced – avoiding a gap in sanctions.

ADM-023.q: An enterprise pays VND 400 million of VAT 15 days late. What is the late-payment interest (VND)?
ADM-023.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Working: 400,000,000 × 0.03% × 15 days = 1,800,000 VND.
Note: Interest runs from the day after the deadline to the day before payment.

ADM-024.q: Household/individual businesses not required to use e-invoices who need an invoice for a transaction must declare and pay tax before the tax authority issues a coded e-invoice for that transaction.
ADM-024.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Household/individual businesses not required to use e-invoices must declare and pay tax first when a customer needs an invoice; the authority then issues a coded e-invoice for that transaction.

ADM-025.q: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP on e-invoices and e-vouchers takes effect on 01/7/2026 and replaces:
ADM-025.e: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP replaces Decree 123/2020/ND-CP, Decree 70/2025/ND-CP and Article 1 of Decree 41/2022/ND-CP.
ADM-025.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Decree 254/2026 replaces Decrees 123/2020, 70/2025 (amending 123) and Article 1 of Decree 41/2022 – consolidating e-invoice and document rules.
Distractors: Decree 125/2020 – penalties (still in force); Decree 126/2020 – tax administration (replaced by Decree 252/2026); Circular 78/2021 – invoice guidance (replaced by Circular 91/2026).

ADM-026.q: The invoicing time for sales of goods is:
o: When ownership or the right to use passes to the buyer, whether or not paid
ADM-026.e: Invoices are issued when ownership or the right to use is transferred.
ADM-026.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Goods invoices are issued on transfer of ownership or right of use, regardless of payment – matching the VAT tax point (VAT-051) and CIT revenue recognition (CIT-014).
Distractors: B, C and D aren't the statutory time.

ADM-027.q: The invoicing time for services is:
o: On completion of the service, whether or not paid; if payment is received before or during the service, at the time of payment (except deposits)
At the end of each quarter
ADM-027.e: The rule on invoicing time for services is retained in Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
ADM-027.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Services: invoice on completion regardless of payment; if paid before or during supply, invoice when payment is received – except deposits (ADM-028).
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

ADM-028.q: Under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP, deposits under the Civil Code to secure service contracts need not be invoiced on receipt, for all types of services.
ADM-028.e: True. Previously this applied only to certain services (accounting, audit, financial/tax advisory, valuation, design…).
ADM-028.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. A Civil Code deposit is security, not payment for the service, so no invoice is issued on receipt. Decree 254/2026 extends this to all services (previously only some professional services).
Note: Clearly distinguish deposits from advances in contracts to avoid late-invoicing findings.

ADM-029.q: The invoicing time for exported goods is:
o: Determined by the seller, but no later than the next working day after customs clearance
The date of the foreign trade contract
The date payment is received from the foreign customer
The date the ship arrives at the importing port
ADM-029.e: The rule from Decree 70/2025/ND-CP is retained.
ADM-029.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP (carrying over Decree 70/2025/ND-CP).
Analysis: For exports, the seller sets the invoice time but no later than the next working day after customs clearance – as final price and quantity are fixed at clearance.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

ADM-030.q: Under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP, sales made between 22:00 and 06:00 by sellers without automatic invoicing software may be invoiced no later than the next working day.
ADM-030.e: True. A new rule easing night-time sales.
ADM-030.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Sellers without automatic invoicing software may issue invoices for 22:00–06:00 transactions by the next working day – easing night-time businesses (restaurants, 24h retail).

ADM-031.q: Medical facilities with hospital-fee software may issue one summary invoice at the end of the day for services where patients do not need an invoice immediately.
ADM-031.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Healthcare facilities with fee-management software may issue one end-of-day summary invoice for services where patients don't request an invoice – fewer small invoices while still capturing revenue.

ADM-032.q: Select ALL cases where an e-invoice is NOT required under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP:
o: Household/individual businesses with income from leasing real estate
Compensation, bonuses, collections and payments on behalf that are not sales revenue
Finished goods given as gifts to customers
Sale of scrap (sawdust, fabric offcuts) to a recycler
ADM-032.e: Gifts of goods and sales of by-products still require invoices.
ADM-032.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: No invoice required: (A) household/individual property rental income (taxed separately); (B) compensation, bonuses and pass-through collections that aren't sales revenue; (C) asset contributions.
Distractors: (D) Gifting finished goods and (E) selling scrap still require invoices (ADM-033).

ADM-033.q: Goods used for promotions, advertising, samples, gifts or in lieu of wages must be invoiced.
ADM-033.e: True. The invoice must show the name, quantity and value of the goods.
ADM-033.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Goods for promotions, advertising, samples, gifts or wages in kind must be invoiced with name, quantity and value – supporting VAT (zero base for lawful promotions – VAT-047) and stock control.

ADM-034.q: Semi-finished castings moved internally from the foundry to the machining workshop of the same company to continue production need not be invoiced.
ADM-034.e: True. Internal transfers to continue production need no invoice; internal documents (internal delivery notes…) are still required.
ADM-034.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Moving semi-finished goods between workshops for further production isn't a sale, so no invoice; internal documents (internal transfer delivery notes) evidence the movement in transit.

ADM-035.q: An e-invoice sent to the buyer has the wrong buyer name and address but the correct tax code and other details. The seller should:
o: Notify the buyer of the error; no need to reissue the invoice
Cancel the invoice and issue a new one dated today
ADM-035.e: Wrong name/address with the correct tax code only requires notification to the buyer (and the tax authority as prescribed).
ADM-035.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: A wrong buyer name or address with the correct tax ID and other details doesn't affect tax → the seller just notifies the buyer (and the authority on the form if required), no re-issue.
Distractors: B is excessive; C – sent invoices can't be cancelled; D – notification is still required.

ADM-036.q: Select ALL errors requiring an adjustment or replacement invoice:
o: Wrong tax rate or tax amount
Goods on the invoice do not match specifications/quality
A spelling error in the street name of the buyer's address (tax code correct)
ADM-036.e: Address errors with the correct tax code only need notification, not adjustment/replacement.
ADM-036.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Adjustment or replacement invoices are needed for errors in: (A) buyer tax ID; (B) amounts; (C) rate or VAT; (D) goods specification or quality – errors affecting tax or transaction value.
Distractors: (E) An address typo with a correct tax ID only needs notification (ADM-035).

ADM-037.q: A seller may delete or cancel an e-invoice already sent to the buyer upon finding an error.
ADM-037.e: False. Errors in invoices already sent must be handled by adjustment or replacement invoices.
ADM-037.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. A sent e-invoice is data already transmitted to the authority; the seller can't delete or cancel it. Errors are fixed by adjustment or replacement invoices (or notification for minor errors).

ADM-038.q: Pre-printed invoices issued by the tax authority cease to be valid from 01/7/2026.
ADM-038.e: True under Article 44(3) of Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; unused invoices must be destroyed as guided.
ADM-038.x:
Basis: Article 44(3) of Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. From 01/07/2026, printed invoices issued by the tax authority expire; unused stock must be destroyed per guidance – completing the move to e-invoices.

ADM-039.q: Until when may self-printed/pre-printed paper receipts be used under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP?
ADM-039.e: Paper receipts may be used until 31/12/2026.
ADM-039.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Paper receipts (self-printed or ordered) may be used until 31/12/2026; from 01/01/2027 only e-receipts – a slower timeline than invoices to let fee collectors prepare.
Distractors: B, C and D have wrong dates.

ADM-040.q: Consumers reporting a seller's failure to issue an invoice, if correct and leading to a penalty, may be rewarded up to 10% of the fine, capped at VND 10 million per case.
ADM-040.x:
Basis: Article 41(1) of Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Consumers reporting a seller's failure to invoice may, if correct and penalised, receive up to 10% of the fine, capped at 10 million VND per case – crowdsourcing invoice compliance.

ADM-041.q: A household business using one tax code for several business locations must show the name and address of each location on the invoice.
ADM-041.e: True per the invoice presentation guidance in Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
ADM-041.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. A household business using one tax ID for several locations must show each location's name and address on invoices – identifying revenue by location and tax jurisdiction.

ADM-042.q: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP expands the services that may be invoiced per data-reconciliation period (no more than 7 days), adding digital platform services, payment intermediaries, insurance, carbon exchanges…
ADM-042.e: True. This helps high-volume sectors invoice in line with practice.
ADM-042.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Services allowed periodic invoicing based on data reconciliation (at most every 7 days) now include digital platforms, payment intermediaries, insurance and carbon exchanges… – suited to high-volume, low-value sectors.

ADM-043.q: An e-invoice with the tax authority's code is:
o: An invoice coded by the tax authority before the seller sends it to the buyer
An invoice with a barcode printed by the seller
An invoice digitally signed by the buyer
ADM-043.e: A non-coded invoice is sent by the seller to the buyer without a tax authority code (for eligible taxpayers).
ADM-043.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A coded invoice receives the authority's code before the seller sends it; an uncoded invoice goes straight to the buyer with data transmitted afterwards (only for eligible – usually large, low-risk – businesses).
Distractors: B, C and D aren't features of coded invoices.

ADM-044.q: E-invoices are accounting documents used directly for bookkeeping and must be kept for at least 10 years under the Accounting Law.
ADM-044.e: True. They are stored electronically and must be retrievable.
ADM-044.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13.
Analysis: True. Invoices are accounting vouchers used directly for bookkeeping, so they must be kept at least 10 years, electronically, with integrity and retrievability (original XML, not just PDF).

ADM-045.q: Match the delay in filing a tax return with the fine for an organisation (no special circumstances):
p: Over 90 days, tax payable, tax and late interest fully paid before a record is made
ADM-045.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Decree 125/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 310/2025/ND-CP).
Analysis: Late filing penalties (organisations): 1–30 days: 2–5 million; 31–60: 5–8 million; 61–90: 8–15 million; over 90 days with tax due but fully paid with interest before the record: 15–25 million. (1–5 days with mitigation: warning – ADM-046.)

ADM-046.q: Filing a tax return 1 to 5 days late with mitigating circumstances is subject to a warning.
ADM-046.x:
Basis: Article 13(1) of Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Filing 1–5 days late with a mitigating circumstance draws only a warning; without one, the 1–30-day band applies.

ADM-047.q: Failing to file a tax return where no tax is payable falls under the VND 8–15 million bracket for organisations.
ADM-047.e: True. The same bracket applies to failing to file the related-party appendix with the CIT finalisation.
ADM-047.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Not filing a return when no tax is due: 8–15 million VND (organisations). The same band applies to omitting the related-party appendix with the CIT return – a reminder not to neglect Appendix I (FCT-073).

ADM-048.q: Incorrect declarations resulting in underpaid tax (not evasion) are fined:
ADM-048.e: 20% of the underdeclared tax, plus full payment of the tax and late-payment interest.
ADM-048.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Incorrect declarations causing underpayment (not evasion): fine of 20% of the shortfall, plus the tax and late-payment interest.
Distractors: B has the wrong rate; C is the evasion penalty; D has no basis.

ADM-049.q: An audit finds an enterprise underdeclared CIT by VND 150 million (not evasion). What is the fine for incorrect declaration (VND)?
ADM-049.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Penalty = 150,000,000 × 20% = 30,000,000 VND, plus the 150 million tax and 0.03%/day interest.

ADM-050.e: Evasion fines range from 1 to 3 times the evaded tax depending on circumstances.
ADM-050.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Evasion (deliberate acts such as using illegal invoices or hiding revenue) is fined 1 to 3 times the evaded tax depending on circumstances; serious cases may be prosecuted.
Distractors: B is the misdeclaration penalty; C is interest; D has no basis.

ADM-051.q: A taxpayer who voluntarily files a supplementary return and pays the tax in full before the tax authority announces an inspection/audit decision is not fined for incorrect declaration (late interest still applies).
ADM-051.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Voluntarily amending and paying in full before an audit decision is announced avoids the misdeclaration penalty; only interest is due – encouraging self-correction.

ADM-052.q: Under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP, multiple instances of issuing invoices at the wrong time in the same case are penalised as one violation, with the bracket based on the total number of invoices.
ADM-052.e: True. Penalties shift from per-invoice to per-violation.
ADM-052.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP amending Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Repeated late invoicing in one case is penalised as a single violation, with the band set by the total number of invoices (ADM-053, ADM-054) – avoiding excessive cumulative fines per invoice.

ADM-053.q: Under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP, issuing one sales invoice at the wrong time (not for internal consumption or promotions) is fined:
ADM-053.e: For internal consumption or promotional goods, one invoice attracts a warning.
ADM-053.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: One late invoice (ordinary): 500,000 – 1,500,000 VND. For internal-use or promotional goods (no tax effect), one invoice draws only a warning.
Distractors: B is for internal/promotional goods; C and D are higher bands.

ADM-054.q: Issuing 100 or more sales invoices at the wrong time is fined in the highest bracket of:
ADM-054.e: The top bracket for wrong-time invoicing under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
ADM-054.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: 100 or more late invoices: the top band of 50–70 million VND (organisations).
Distractors: B and C are lower bands; D isn't in the rules.

ADM-055.q: Failing to issue one invoice for an ordinary sale under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP is fined:
ADM-055.e: Fines rise with the number of invoices not issued, up to VND 60–80 million.
ADM-055.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Failing to issue one invoice (ordinary): 1–2 million VND – heavier than late invoicing as revenue may be hidden; bands rise with the number, up to 60–80 million.
Distractors: B and C are late-invoicing levels; D is a high-volume band.

ADM-056.q: Under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP, violations with 2 or more mitigating circumstances take the minimum of the bracket; with 2 or more aggravating circumstances, the maximum.
ADM-056.e: True. The rule clarifies how brackets are applied.
ADM-056.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Two or more mitigating circumstances → the band minimum; two or more aggravating → the maximum; otherwise the midpoint – clarifying application and limiting discretion.

ADM-057.q: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP amending Decree 125/2020/ND-CP takes effect from 16/01/2026.
ADM-057.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 310/2025 was issued on 02/12/2025 and took effect on 16/01/2026, amending Decree 125/2020 on tax and invoice penalties (per-violation fines, invoice-count bands, aggravation/mitigation).

ADM-058.q: Match the conduct of related organisations/individuals with the fine under Decree 310/2025/ND-CP:
p: Providing information 5 or more days late
Providing inaccurate information on accounts, assets, income
ADM-058.e: Sanctions on third parties obliged to provide information and on invoice trading.
ADM-058.x:
Basis: Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Third parties: information 5 or more days late: 2–6 million; inaccurate account, asset or income data: 6–10 million; failure to provide: 10–16 million. Buying, selling or giving invoices: 20–50 million (below criminal level).

ADM-059.q: Fines for organisations are twice those for individuals; household businesses are fined at half the organisation level.
ADM-059.e: True under the fine principles of Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
ADM-059.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The decree's amounts apply to organisations; individuals pay half (organisations pay double); household businesses are treated like individuals – half the organisation level.

ADM-060.q: From 01/01/2026, the presumptive (lump-sum) tax method for household/individual businesses ends.
ADM-060.e: True. Household/individual businesses move to self-declaration and self-payment.
ADM-060.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. From 01/01/2026 presumptive (lump-sum) tax ends; household/individual businesses self-declare on actual revenue, with e-invoices or cash registers above the threshold – making the sector's revenue transparent.

ADM-061.q: The business licence fee is abolished from 01/01/2026.
ADM-061.e: True. Enterprises and household businesses no longer declare or pay the licence fee from 2026.
ADM-061.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. The business licence fee is abolished from 01/01/2026 – enterprises and household businesses no longer file or pay it, cutting compliance costs especially for start-ups and small households.

ADM-062.q: From the 2026 tax period, household/individual businesses do not pay VAT or PIT when annual revenue is:
ADM-062.e: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP (amending Decree 68/2026/ND-CP) raised the threshold from 500 million to 1 billion per year.
ADM-062.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: From 2026, household/individual businesses with annual revenue ≤ 1 billion pay no VAT or PIT (Decree 141/2026 raised it from 500 million – VAT-009, PIT-084).
Distractors: 500 and 200 million are old thresholds; 3 billion is a method grouping point.

ADM-063.q: How does a household business with annual revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion notify revenue to the tax authority under Decree 141/2026/ND-CP (operating from the start of the year)?
o: Twice: by 31/7 (first half) and by 31/01 of the following year
ADM-063.e: Businesses starting in the second half of the year notify once, by 31/01 of the following year.
ADM-063.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP (amending Decree 68/2026/ND-CP).
Analysis: Household businesses with revenue ≤ 1 billion operating from the start of the year report revenue twice: by 31/07 (first half) and by 31/01 of the next year (full year). Those starting in H2 report once by 31/01 – letting the authority monitor threshold breaches.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

ADM-064.q: A household business whose revenue exceeds VND 1 billion switches to quarterly filing from the quarter in which revenue exceeds the threshold and must use e-invoices.
ADM-064.e: True. It must register for e-invoices within 30 days from the end of the tax period in which cumulative revenue exceeds 1 billion.
ADM-064.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Once cumulative revenue exceeds 1 billion, the household business files quarterly from that quarter and registers for e-invoices within 30 days after the end of the period in which the threshold was crossed.

ADM-065.q: Enterprises/organisations with total annual revenue of VND 1 billion or less are CIT-exempt and need not make provisional payments; those operating less than 12 months annualise revenue.
ADM-065.e: True. Not applicable to subsidiaries/associates of enterprises that do not meet the conditions.
ADM-065.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Enterprises with annual revenue ≤ 1 billion are CIT-exempt and needn't pay provisionally; a short year is annualised (CIT-102). Subsidiaries/affiliates of ineligible enterprises are excluded (CIT-104).

ADM-066.q: Import-stage VAT is not eligible for deferral under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
ADM-066.e: True. Tax deferral decrees do not cover import-stage VAT.
ADM-066.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP on tax payment deferral.
Analysis: True. Import VAT is paid per customs declaration and tied to clearance; deferral decrees (including 245/2026) cover domestic VAT, CIT, PIT, land rent… but not import-stage tax.

ADM-067.q: During the deferral period under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP, no late-payment interest is charged on the deferred tax.
ADM-067.e: True. If the system has charged interest, the tax authority will adjust it.
ADM-067.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Deferral moves the payment deadline, so no late-payment interest accrues on deferred amounts during the period; system-generated interest is reversed. Interest starts if unpaid after the extended deadline.

ADM-068.q: Select ALL taxpayers eligible for deferral under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP (if conditions are met):
o: Enterprises in sectors listed in Appendix I (agriculture, processing, transport…)
Enterprises with several activities, one of which is in Appendix I
ADM-068.e: An enterprise with one Appendix I activity is deferred for all tax payable; import-stage VAT is not deferred.
ADM-068.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Eligible: (A) enterprises in Appendix I sectors (agriculture, processing, transport…); (B) small and micro enterprises; (C) multi-activity enterprises with one Appendix I activity – deferral covers all their tax due.
Distractors: (D) Import VAT isn't deferrable (ADM-066).

ADM-069.q: The deferral period for VAT of May 2026 under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP is:
ADM-069.e: May 2026 VAT is deferred 5 months, due 20/11/2026.
ADM-069.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: VAT for May 2026 (original deadline 20/06/2026) is deferred 5 months → new deadline 20/11/2026. Other periods have their own deferral lengths in the Decree.
Distractors: 3, 6 and 1 months don't match May.

ADM-070.q: The taxpayer submits one deferral request for all eligible tax and land rent; the tax authority need not notify acceptance.
ADM-070.e: True. Taxpayers should keep proof of timely submission.
ADM-070.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. One deferral request covers all eligible taxes and land rent; the authority issues no acceptance notice – the taxpayer bears responsibility for eligibility. Keep proof of timely submission and eligibility evidence.

ADM-071.q: Under the 2025 Tax Administration Law, household/individual businesses determine their own revenue to declare and pay tax periodically, instead of the tax authority assessing a lump-sum amount.
ADM-071.e: True. The tax authority provides data and apps to support self-declaration.
ADM-071.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Presumptive tax ends (ADM-060); household/individual businesses self-determine actual revenue and file periodically. The authority shifts to support: data, apps (eTax Mobile), cash-register invoices.

ADM-072.q: The deadline for the September 2026 VAT return (monthly filer) is:
ADM-072.e: Monthly filing: by the 20th of the following month.
ADM-072.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly filing is due by the 20th of the next month → September 2026 is due 20/10/2026 (Tuesday, a working day).
Distractors: B and C are the Q3 quarterly deadline; D has no basis.

ADM-073.q: Select ALL checks to perform when receiving input e-invoices:
o: Verify the invoice on the tax authority's e-invoice portal
Check the seller's tax code status (active, not ceased, not absconded)
Match the invoice with the contract, purchase order and goods receipt
Ensure non-cash payment for invoices of VND 5 million or more
Only require the seller's red seal on the invoice
ADM-073.e: E-invoices do not need seals; verifying data on the tax authority's system is the core control.
ADM-073.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Input invoice controls: (A) look up the invoice on the tax portal; (B) check the seller's tax ID status; (C) match to contract, order, goods receipt; (D) ensure non-cash payment for invoices of 5 million or more.
Distractors: (E) E-invoices need no stamp; a 'red seal' proves nothing.

ADM-074.q: Invoices issued by a seller after its tax code has been notified as ceased or terminated are illegal invoices.
ADM-074.e: True. The buyer cannot deduct VAT or claim the expense and may be penalised.
ADM-074.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Invoices issued after the seller's tax ID was suspended or terminated are illegal; the buyer can't credit VAT or deduct the cost and may be fined (ADM-075). Unlike invoices issued before the notice (ADM-114).

ADM-075.q: Select ALL consequences for a buyer using illegal invoices:
o: Must file supplementary returns, pay tax and late interest; may be penalised
Ignored if paid by bank transfer
ADM-075.e: Bank transfer payment does not legitimise an illegal invoice.
ADM-075.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Consequences: (A) no input VAT credit; (B) no CIT deduction; (C) amend, pay tax and interest, possibly fines (20% misdeclaration or 1–3× evasion depending on intent).
Distractors: (D) Bank payment is only one credit condition; it doesn't legitimise an illegal invoice.

ADM-076.q: E-invoices do not require the buyer's digital signature (unless agreed by the parties).
ADM-076.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. E-invoices require the seller's digital signature; the buyer's isn't required unless agreed (e.g., large transactions needing two-party confirmation).

ADM-077.q: Enterprises should periodically review the tax code status of suppliers (especially new suppliers and large transactions) to prevent invoice risks.
ADM-077.e: True. This is a key preventive control for purchasing and accounting.
ADM-077.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; COSO 2013 (control activities).
Analysis: True. Periodic checks of suppliers' tax ID status are a preventive control – reducing exposure to invoices from vanished or inactive entities, especially new suppliers and large purchases.

ADM-078.q: An enterprise files a tax return 20 days late with no mitigating or aggravating circumstances. What is the specific fine (the average of the VND 2–5 million bracket) (VND)?
ADM-078.e: Average of the bracket: (2 + 5) / 2 = 3.5 million VND.
ADM-078.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 20 days late is the 1–30-day band: 2–5 million. No circumstances → midpoint = (2 + 5) / 2 = 3.5 million VND.

ADM-079.q: Late-payment interest is not an administrative penalty, but enterprises must still pay it when paying tax late.
ADM-079.e: True. It compensates for use of tax money, at 0.03% per day.
ADM-079.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Late-payment interest (0.03%/day) compensates for using tax money; it isn't an administrative penalty and is due even when no fine applies (e.g., voluntary amendment – ADM-051).

ADM-080.q: Overpaid tax may be offset against outstanding or future tax, or refunded as prescribed.
ADM-080.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Overpaid tax may be offset against debts or later liabilities, or refunded – the taxpayer's choice under tax procedures.

ADM-081.q: Select ALL cases in which the tax authority may assess tax:
o: Failure to register or declare tax as required
Failure to keep books, invoices and documents, or incomplete records
Transaction prices inconsistent with normal market values
Failure to comply with an audit/inspection decision
Timely, complete declarations with supporting records
ADM-081.e: Tax assessment applies when taxpayers do not correctly determine their own obligations.
ADM-081.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Assessment applies when: (A) no registration or return; (B) missing or incomplete books and documents; (C) transaction prices inconsistent with market values; (D) non-compliance with audit decisions.
Distractors: (E) Timely, complete, documented returns give no basis for assessment.

ADM-082.q: Household businesses with revenue under VND 1 billion/year, though not paying VAT or PIT, still need to record revenue and notify it as prescribed.
ADM-082.e: True. Revenue data determine when the threshold is exceeded.
ADM-082.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Below the 1 billion threshold, household businesses still keep revenue records and report revenue (ADM-063) – this data shows when the threshold is crossed and tax obligations begin.

ADM-083.q: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP adds simultaneous tax examinations under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MAAC) to which Vietnam is a party.
ADM-083.e: True. It supports international tax cooperation, especially with multinational groups.
ADM-083.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; MAAC Convention (OECD).
Analysis: True. Decree 252/2026 adds simultaneous tax examinations under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance – enabling coordinated audits of multinationals with foreign tax authorities.

ADM-084.q: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP adds a priority regime for qualifying taxpayers (form, scope and conditions of priority).
ADM-084.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. A priority regime (forms, scope, conditions) for compliant taxpayers – e.g., faster procedures, refund-first-audit-later – encourages voluntary compliance in a risk-based model.

ADM-085.q: Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, an enterprise not operating at its registered address that fails to restore or terminate its tax code within 120 days of notice may have exit bans imposed on its legal representative and beneficial owners.
ADM-085.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Businesses that abandon their registered address and don't restore or terminate their tax ID within 120 days of notice may face exit bans on the legal representative and beneficial owner – a strong tool against shell companies and invoice trading.

ADM-086.q: Under Official Letter 13203/NBI-QLDN3 (07/10/2026), an e-invoice that was coded and sent to the buyer but then mistakenly cancelled when submitting Form 04/SS-HĐĐT:
ADM-086.e: A cancelled invoice is no longer valid; the business issues a new replacement invoice per Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
o: Is no longer valid; the business issues a new replacement invoice
Remains valid because the buyer received it
Can be restored by the tax authority on request
ADM-086.x:
Basis: Official Letter 13203/NBI-QLDN3 of 07/10/2026; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: An invoice notified as cancelled via Form 04/SS-HĐĐT (even by mistake) is void; the business issues a new replacement invoice under Circular 91/2026.
Distractors: B – buyer receipt doesn't restore it; C – there's no restoration procedure; D – it must be re-issued to record the sale.

ADM-087.q: Under Official Letter 7371/CT-QLNT (05/10/2026), errors in e-invoices are handled under:
ADM-087.e: The Tax Department applies rules by invoice date: before 01/7/2026 under Decree 123/2020 (amended by 70/2025); from 01/7/2026 under Circular 91/2026.
o: Article 19 of Decree 123/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 70/2025/ND-CP) for invoices issued before 01/7/2026; Article 10 of Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC for invoices issued from 01/7/2026
ADM-087.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7371/CT-QLNT of 05/10/2026.
Analysis: The rule depends on the invoice date: invoices issued before 01/07/2026 are corrected under Article 19 of Decree 123/2020 (amended by Decree 70/2025); from 01/07/2026 under Article 10 of Circular 91/2026.
Distractors: B and C apply one text to all; D is wrong as errors must be fixed.

ADM-088.q: Under Official Letter 7336/CT-QLNT (02/10/2026), household businesses can look up individual e-invoices on hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn without logging in, by entering full invoice details.
ADM-088.e: True. For fuller data, log in to the e-invoice system or the eTax Mobile app.
ADM-088.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7336/CT-QLNT of 02/10/2026.
Analysis: True. Individual invoices can be checked on hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn without login by entering full invoice details. Aggregate data (purchase/sales lists) requires login or eTax Mobile.

ADM-089.q: Under Official Letter 7478/CT-QLNT (08/10/2026), when a car or motorbike is sold to a buyer who must register ownership and the e-invoice shows full identifiers (chassis/engine numbers, make, year…):
ADM-089.e: Under Article 11(10) of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, complete invoice data let the tax authority determine the registration fee; sales to dealers for resale need not show these identifiers.
o: The tax authority computes the registration fee and notifies; the buyer does not file a registration fee return
The buyer still files the registration fee return
The seller pays the fee on behalf
ADM-089.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7478/CT-QLNT of 08/10/2026; Article 11(10) of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: When the vehicle sales invoice shows full identification (chassis, engine numbers, brand, year…), the authority computes and notifies registration fees; the buyer files no declaration. Sales to resellers needn't show these fields.
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

ADM-090.q: Under Official Letter 7364/CT-CĐS (10/2026), the Tax Department launched an AI assistant on eTax Mobile and the tax public service portal, answering in Vietnamese and English with citations to articles and clauses.
ADM-090.e: True. The chatbot supports queries on tax, fees and invoices by text or voice; taxpayers should still check the original texts.
ADM-090.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7364/CT-CĐS (10/2026).
Analysis: True. The AI assistant on eTax Mobile and the tax public-service portal answers in Vietnamese and English with article references. Answers are supportive only; check the original texts before relying on them.

ADM-091.q: The deadline for the November 2026 VAT return of a monthly filer (20/12/2026 is a Sunday) is:
ADM-091.e: A 20th that falls on Sunday moves to the next working day: 21/12/2026.
ADM-091.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: November 2026 is due 20/12/2026 (Sunday) → moves to Monday 21/12/2026.
Distractors: B ignores the shift; C – filing early isn't required; D has no basis.

ADM-092.q: The Q4/2026 VAT return deadline (31/01/2027 is a Sunday) is:
ADM-092.e: Quarterly: the last day of the first month of the next quarter; falling on Sunday, it moves to 01/02/2027.
ADM-092.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: Q4/2026 is due on the last day of the next quarter's first month = 31/01/2027 (Sunday) → Monday 01/02/2027.
Distractors: B doesn't shift; C and D confuse it with monthly filing.

ADM-093.q: An audit finds an enterprise underdeclared VAT by VND 80 million, paid 100 days late. What is the total of the incorrect-declaration fine and late-payment interest (VND)?
ADM-093.e: Fine 20% × 80 = 16 million; interest 80,000,000 × 0.03% × 100 = 2.4 million. Total 18.4 million VND.
ADM-093.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Working: Penalty = 20% × 80 = 16 million. Interest = 80,000,000 × 0.03% × 100 = 2.4 million. Total 18.4 million VND (excluding the 80 million tax).

ADM-094.q: Match each type of return with its deadline:
ADM-094.e: Basic filing deadlines under the Tax Administration Law and guidance.
p: Last day of the first month of the next quarter
Last day of the 3rd month after year-end
Last day of the 4th month after the calendar year
ADM-094.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Monthly – the 20th of the next month; quarterly – last day of the next quarter's first month; corporate annual finalisation – last day of the third month after year-end; individual PIT self-filing – last day of the fourth month. Days off shift to the next working day.

ADM-095.q: When a supplementary return increases tax payable, the taxpayer must compute and pay late-payment interest from the day after the original period's payment deadline.
ADM-095.e: True. Interest accrues on the additional tax from the day after the original deadline to the day before payment.
ADM-095.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. For upward amendments, interest accrues on the additional tax from the day after the original deadline of the erroneous period to the day before payment – as that tax was due from the original deadline.

ADM-096.q: An e-invoice must carry the seller's digital signature; an invoice without a red seal is still valid.
ADM-096.e: True. E-invoices use digital/electronic signatures; no seal is required.
ADM-096.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. E-invoices are authenticated by the seller's digital/electronic signature; no stamp is required. A PDF view without a red seal is valid if the electronic data is valid.

ADM-097.q: Select ALL items normally mandatory on an electronic VAT invoice:
ADM-097.e: The bank account number is not a mandatory invoice field.
o: Buyer's name, address, tax code (or ID number)
Goods description, unit, quantity, unit price, amount, tax rate, tax amount
Seller's digital signature, time of issuance
ADM-097.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Usual mandatory content: (A) seller details; (B) buyer details (tax ID or personal ID); (C) goods, quantity, unit price, amount, rate, VAT; (D) seller's digital signature and issue time.
Distractors: (E) The buyer's bank account isn't mandatory.

ADM-098.q: Under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP, when selling to a non-business individual, the invoice may show the buyer's personal ID number instead of a tax code.
ADM-098.e: True. Personal ID numbers have replaced individual tax codes since 01/7/2025; the invoice shows the ID number if the buyer provides it.
ADM-098.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 86/2024/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Since 01/07/2025 the personal ID replaces individual tax IDs (ADM-021); for non-business individual buyers who provide it, invoices show the personal ID – linking spending data to individuals (e.g., medical and education deductions).

ADM-099.q: An enterprise issued an invoice on 10/10/2026 with an overstated unit price. On 25/10/2026 the parties agree to issue a downward adjustment invoice. The VAT adjustment is declared in:
ADM-099.e: Adjustment invoices are declared in the period they are issued; here both fall in October 2026.
o: The period of the adjustment invoice (October 2026)
The original invoice period via a supplementary return
ADM-099.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Adjustment invoices are declared in the period they're issued (no amendment of the original period). Here both are in October 2026, so October.
Distractors: B uses an unnecessary amendment; C is the wrong period; D is wrong as the adjustment must be declared.

ADM-100.q: Buyers are responsible for checking the legality of input invoices; using illegal invoices may be penalised even if fully paid.
ADM-100.e: True. Buyers should verify invoices, the seller's status and the underlying transaction.
ADM-100.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Buyers must verify input invoices (lookup, seller status, real transaction); using illegal invoices can be penalised even if fully paid (ADM-075).

ADM-101.q: Select ALL red flags on input invoices that accounting should review:
ADM-101.e: The first four are common in invoice-trading cases; long-standing compliant suppliers are low-risk.
o: A newly established supplier with small capital issuing very large invoices
Registered business lines inconsistent with the goods sold
Payment to a personal account rather than the seller's company account
Delivery address/transport documents inconsistent with the invoice
A long-standing supplier with a good compliance record and stable transactions
ADM-101.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; ACFE (procurement fraud indicators).
Analysis: Red flags: (A) new, thinly capitalised suppliers issuing huge invoices; (B) registered sector inconsistent with goods; (C) payment to personal accounts; (D) transport documents or delivery addresses not matching – typical of invoice trading.
Distractors: (E) Long-standing, compliant suppliers are low risk.

ADM-102.q: A household business files a tax return 40 days late. The organisation bracket is VND 5–8 million; the average applies. What is the fine for the household business (VND)?
ADM-102.e: Average for organisations = 6.5 million; household businesses pay half the organisation fine: 3.25 million VND.
ADM-102.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 310/2025/ND-CP).
Working: 40 days late is the 31–60-day band: 5–8 million (organisations). Midpoint = 6.5 million. Household businesses pay half = 3.25 million VND.

ADM-103.q: The statute of limitations for penalising procedural tax violations is 2 years from the date of the violation.
ADM-103.e: True. For incorrect declarations and evasion it is 5 years; procedural violations 2 years.
ADM-103.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The limitation period for procedural violations (late filing, registration…) is 2 years from the act; for misdeclaration and evasion it's 5 years (ADM-104). Past the limit no fine applies, but unpaid tax is still due.

ADM-104.q: The statute of limitations for penalising tax evasion and incorrect declarations causing underpayment is:
ADM-104.e: Evasion and underdeclaration have a 5-year limitation period.
ADM-104.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: The limitation period for evasion and misdeclaration causing underpayment is 5 years from the act – aligned with the 2025 Law's 5-year amendment window (ADM-003).
Distractors: 2 years is for procedural violations; 10 and 1 years are wrong.

ADM-105.q: Arrange the input-invoice control steps before recording:
ADM-105.e: Invoice control flow: technical → seller → real transaction → payment → recording.
o: Receive the e-invoice, check digital signature and tax authority code
Check the seller's tax code status
Match the invoice with the PO, goods receipt and acceptance minutes
Check the non-cash payment condition (from VND 5 million)
ADM-105.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Control sequence: (1) technical – signature, authority code; (2) seller tax ID status; (3) match to the real transaction – order, receipt, acceptance; (4) non-cash payment condition; (5) approve, post, declare. From form to substance before recording.

ADM-106.q: From 2026, enterprises no longer declare or pay the business licence fee.
ADM-106.e: True. Resolution 198/2025/QH15 abolished the licence fee from 01/01/2026.
ADM-106.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. The licence fee was abolished from 01/01/2026 (ADM-061) – no return or payment from 2026; prior years' arrears follow the old rules.

ADM-107.q: An enterprise files a supplementary return increasing 2025 CIT by VND 50 million (original deadline 31/3/2026) and pays on 30/9/2026. Late days are 182. What is the late-payment interest (VND)?
ADM-107.e: 50,000,000 × 0.03% × 182 = 2,730,000 VND (no incorrect-declaration fine if filed before an audit decision).
ADM-107.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Working: 50,000,000 × 0.03% × 182 days = 2,730,000 VND. Being a voluntary amendment before an audit decision, no misdeclaration penalty applies (ADM-051).

ADM-108.q: Under the 2025 Tax Administration Law, how long after the original filing deadline may a supplementary return be filed?
ADM-108.e: Law 108/2025/QH15 shortens the period to 5 years (before an inspection/audit decision is announced).
ADM-108.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: The amendment window is 5 years from the original filing deadline, before an audit decision is announced (ADM-003).
Distractors: 10 years is the 2019 Law; 3 and 2 years are wrong.

ADM-109.q: E-invoices generated from cash registers connected to the tax authority do not require a digital signature.
ADM-109.e: True. This feature of cash-register invoices enables fast retail invoicing.
ADM-109.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Invoices generated by cash registers connected to the tax authority needn't carry a digital signature – data is transmitted directly, ensuring authenticity, and retail can invoice each sale quickly.

ADM-110.q: Match each invoice error (issued from 01/7/2026) with its treatment:
ADM-110.e: Summary of e-invoice error handling under Decree 254/2026 and Circular 91/2026, plus Official Letter 13203/NBI-QLDN3.
p: Wrong buyer name, correct tax code
Issue an adjustment or replacement invoice
Invoice sent to buyer mistakenly cancelled
ADM-110.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC; Official Letter 13203/NBI-QLDN3.
Analysis: Wrong name, correct tax ID – notify, no re-issue (ADM-035). Wrong amount or rate – adjust/replace (ADM-036). Mistakenly cancelled sent invoice – new replacement invoice (ADM-086). Partial return – downward adjustment invoice.

ADM-111.q: On 16/10/2026 the Tax Department said the MOF is reporting to the competent authority on amending PIT rules for household businesses with revenue above VND 3 billion; until amended, current rules still apply.
ADM-111.e: True. It is only a proposal; current rules (income method, documented deductible expenses) still apply.
ADM-111.x:
Basis: Tax Department statement of 16/10/2026; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The proposed change to PIT for household businesses above 3 billion isn't in force; meanwhile the current rules apply (income method, valid expenses – PIT-085). Principle: a policy proposal isn't a legal basis.

ADM-112.q: Select ALL enforcement measures for tax administrative decisions:
ADM-112.e: Tax rates are set by law, not enforcement measures.
o: Deducting money from the taxpayer's bank account
Deducting part of salary or income
ADM-112.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Enforcement measures: (A) deducting from bank accounts; (B) suspending invoice use; (C) garnishing wages or income; (D) seizing and auctioning assets (plus others like licence revocation).
Distractors: (E) Tax rates are statutory, not an enforcement tool.

ADM-113.q: Under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP, sellers must issue invoices when dispatching goods for lending, borrowing or returning goods.
ADM-113.e: True. Lending, borrowing and returning goods require invoices as prescribed.
ADM-113.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Lending, borrowing or returning goods requires an invoice – goods actually move between parties, needing documents for control and any tax consequences.

ADM-114.q: An enterprise is notified that a supplier is 'not operating at its registered address'. Invoices issued before the tax authority's notice:
ADM-114.e: Invoices issued before the notice are not automatically illegal; the buyer must prove the transaction is real. Invoices issued after the tax code ceased are illegal.
o: May still be used if the transaction is real, documented and paid properly, but transaction evidence should be kept
ADM-114.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Invoices issued before the authority announced the supplier's absence from its address aren't automatically illegal; the buyer may use them if the transaction is real, documented and properly paid – keeping evidence (contract, transport, receipt). Only invoices after the tax ID suspension are illegal (ADM-074).
Distractors: B and C are too strict; D is irrelevant.

ADM-115.e: Invoices already sent cannot be cancelled at will; use adjustment or replacement invoices.
o: Tax-authority pre-printed invoices are no longer valid.
Paper receipts may be used until 31/12/2026.
Sellers may freely cancel invoices already sent and reissue.
Deposits securing service contracts need not be invoiced on receipt.
ADM-115.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – authority-printed invoices expire from 01/07/2026 (ADM-038). (2) True – paper receipts until 31/12/2026 (ADM-039). (3) False – sent invoices can't be cancelled at will (ADM-037). (4) True – service deposits aren't invoiced on receipt (ADM-028).

ADM-116.q: A quarterly filer does not file monthly VAT returns within that quarter.
ADM-116.e: True. The VAT filing period is fixed as quarterly or monthly for the calendar year.
ADM-116.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. The VAT filing period is fixed for the whole year (ADM-013); quarterly filers submit only the quarterly return, not monthly returns within it.

ADM-117.q: An enterprise is found to have evaded VND 60 million of tax, fined at 1 times the evaded tax. What is the total of evaded tax and fine (excluding late interest) (VND million)?
ADM-117.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Evaded tax 60 million + fine of 1× = 60 million → 120 million VND (excluding interest).
Note: 1× is the minimum; aggravating factors can raise it to 3× (a 180 million fine).

ADM-118.q: Commercial banks must provide taxpayers' account information to the tax authority as prescribed; incorrect provision may be penalised.
ADM-118.e: True. Decree 310/2025/ND-CP adds fines for third parties providing information late, not at all or inaccurately.
ADM-118.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Commercial banks must provide taxpayers' account information to the authority as required; late, missing or inaccurate data is fined under the third-party bands (ADM-058).

ADM-119.q: For Q2/2026 provisional CIT eligible for deferral under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP, how is late-payment interest treated during the deferral?
ADM-119.e: Deferred tax bears no late-payment interest during the deferral period.
ADM-119.x:
Basis: Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Deferred Q2/2026 provisional CIT bears no late-payment interest during the deferral (ADM-067).
Distractors: B and C wrongly charge interest; D – there's no violation to penalise.

ADM-120.q: From 01/7/2026, electronically stored tax returns and e-invoices must ensure integrity, retrievability and the retention period under the Accounting Law.
ADM-120.e: True. Invoices are accounting documents; electronic storage must meet security, integrity and retrieval requirements.
ADM-120.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Electronically stored returns and e-invoices must remain intact (unaltered), retrievable and kept for the Accounting Law period (bookkeeping invoices: at least 10 years – ADM-044).

ADM-121.q: Select ALL taxes declared per transaction:
ADM-121.e: Enterprise VAT is filed monthly/quarterly; the others are per transaction.
o: FCT withheld and paid by the Vietnamese party
ADM-121.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Per-transaction filing: (A) contractor tax withheld by the Vietnamese party (FCT-016); (B) PIT on property transfers; (C) registration fees.
Distractors: (D) Enterprises' VAT is filed monthly or quarterly.

ADM-122.q: Refund claims subject to pre-refund examination include first-time refund claims (with some exceptions) and high-risk cases under risk management criteria.
ADM-122.e: True. Claims are classified as refund-first or examine-first based on risk criteria and compliance history.
ADM-122.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Refund files are split into refund-first-audit-later (compliant, low risk) and audit-first-refund-later (first-time claims – with exceptions, high-risk profiles, prior violations…).

ADM-123.q: An enterprise owes VND 900 million in tax and pays another 450 million. Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, what is the remaining debt and does it qualify for lifting the exit ban (threshold below 500 million)? Enter the remaining debt.
ADM-123.e: Remaining 900 − 450 = 450 million < 500 million with partial payment made → qualifies for lifting the exit ban.
ADM-123.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Remaining debt = 900 − 450 = 450 million < 500 million (enterprise threshold), with part paid → the exit ban can be lifted (ADM-018).

ADM-124.q: An export-processing enterprise that changes its objective to one without non-tariff-zone treatment during investment must adjust/replace invoices issued; from 01/7/2026 under Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
ADM-124.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7552/CT-QLNT of 12/10/2026; Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. When an export processing enterprise loses non-tariff-zone status during investment, invoices issued under the old regime (e.g., 0% for sales into the zone) must be adjusted or replaced; from 01/07/2026 under Circular 91/2026.

ADM-125.q: The circular guiding e-invoices and e-vouchers effective from 01/7/2026 is:
ADM-125.e: Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC guides Decree 254/2026/ND-CP on invoices and e-vouchers.
ADM-125.x:
Basis: Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Circular 91/2026 guides Decree 254/2026 on e-invoices and documents from 01/07/2026, replacing Circular 78/2021.
Distractors: Circular 78/2021 – superseded; Circular 80/2021 – tax administration (replaced by Circular 89/2026); Circular 32/2025 – not the Decree 254 invoice guidance.
